# TEI fixtures

Test fixtures for reading TEI XML editions (`src/engine/hermes/tei.js`, `test/hermes-tei.test.js`).
One is a real EpiDoc edition, copied unchanged; six are constructed, and say so. No Perseus text is
committed (Perseus's TEI is CC BY-SA): the TEI P4 fixture is constructed, and a real Perseus P4 file
is checked only locally, by `scripts/check-perseus-p4.mjs` (opt-in: `PERSEUS_P4_FILE`).

| File | Where it comes from | Licence | What it exercises |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isicily-ISic000934.xml` | [ISicily/ISicily](https://github.com/ISicily/ISicily), `inscriptions/ISic000934.xml`, commit `d3ebc63ff30b3b3b7359513292a5e7b01a05af7c`. I.Sicily's EpiDoc edition of the epitaph of Zodoros (Syracuse, 4th to 6th century CE), edited by Jonathan Prag. Copied unchanged. | CC BY 4.0 (the repository's `licence.txt`, and the file's own `<licence>`) | A real EpiDoc file: a Greek place name broken over three lines within words (`lb break="no"`); a place name in the English commentary, which is the editors' words because the file has a `div type="edition"`; `<geo>` written with a comma (`37.08415, 15.27628`); place names with a ref in the teiHeader (where the stone was made and found), which are not converted; the edition's URI, DOI, editor, licence, and the museum and inventory number of the stone |
| `keys-constructed.xml` | Constructed | As below | Place names with a key and no ref (`test/tei-reading.test.js`): keys in Perseus's manner (`key="tgn,7011179"`, Getty TGN, the prefix before a comma) and EpiDoc's (`key="pleiades:579885"`), one out of shape (`pleiades:athens`), one with no prefix (`Q1524`), one with a prefix no gazetteer is known by (`perseus,Argos`), and a ref with a key beside it |
| `p4-constructed.xml` | Constructed, in the manner of a digital library's TEI P4 Latin prose text, with invented words, names of people and institutions; not copied from any edition | Constructed for these tests; no licence needed | TEI P4 (`test/tei-p4.test.js`): `<!DOCTYPE TEI.2 PUBLIC "-//TEI P4//DTD Main Document Type//EN" …>` whose internal subset declares and uses external parameter entities (`%ISOlat1;`, `%ISOgrk1;`), so the ISO entities are read (`&aelig;`, `&Agr;&thgr;&eegr;&ngr;&agr;&igr;`), and an entity of its own (`&responsibility;`); `TEI.2 id`; a header in the P4 manner (sponsor, principal, funder, extent, a `biblStruct` source, a `refsDecl`, a `revisionDesc`, an `idno type="URI"`); `<language id>` in the `langUsage`, one with an `ident`, two whose ids are not tags; `text lang="la"`; `div1`/`div2` with `milestone unit="section"`; Latin place names with `key="tgn,…"` and no ref, one with `reg`, one with an `id`; a Greek name in Beta Code (`*)aqh=nai`) and the same name in Greek letters; a `note resp="ed"` |
| `p4-boilerplate-constructed.xml` | Constructed, in the manner of a digital library's TEI P4 header, with invented words; not copied from any edition | Constructed for these tests; no licence needed | TEI P4 header boilerplate (`test/tei-p4.test.js`): a DOCTYPE naming an outside DTD, and entities only that DTD would declare, never declared in the file and not ISO's (`&responsibility;` twice, `&fund.NEH;`, `&Perseus.publish;` in place of the publicationStmt's publisher); two Latin place names with `key="tgn,…"`. The tests vary it: an entity in a place name's words, key or ref, or in a listed place's idno; in the title or the edition's idno; the entities declared; no DOCTYPE |
| `prose-constructed.xml` | Constructed | Constructed for these tests; no licence needed | A prose edition: `div type="book"`, `div type="chapter"`, `pb n`, `milestone unit="section"`; a main title after a subtitle; author, publisher, date, a DOI as the only address, a licence, a `sourceDesc/bibl`; a place name with a key and a note inside it; a ref with two web addresses; a place name with no ref; a `<settlement>` inside a referenced `<placeName>`; a place name in a note; an `xml:id` |
| `verse-constructed.xml` | Constructed | As above | A verse edition: `l n`; `<rs type="place">`, `<name type="place">`, `<region ref>`; `<rs type="person">`, which is not read; `xml:lang` inherited from `<text>`, and an `xml:lang="Latin"` that is not a language tag; no address for the edition; a licence in words only |
| `pointers-constructed.xml` | Constructed | As above | Every kind of ref: a `prefixDef` that expands to a web address, one that expands to a `urn:`, a prefix with no `prefixDef`, a `urn:`; local refs to a `<listPlace>` in the header (one web address; two, which is ambiguous; none) and to one in `<back>`, after the place name; a ref to an id that is not there; a ref into another file; place names with no ref, with and without a key; `<choice>` (`orig`/`reg`, `abbr`/`expan`, `sic`/`corr`) and `<app>` (`lem`/`rdg`); two originals in the `sourceDesc` |
| `whg-constructed.xml` | Constructed | As above | World Historical Gazetteer addresses (`src/engine/hermes/addresses.js`): a reconciliation id `place:gn:…` and an entity page, both rewritten to `https://w3id.org/whg/id/place:…`; a cluster address in the range of whg_ids, kept; a database-record address and a staging address, refused; a `<listPlace>` idno in the `place:gn:…` form and one on staging; `@cert`, `@type`, `@resp` on place names and `@type` on a place; a place's `<desc>` and `<note>` |

## Excerpts from real editions

`excerpts/` holds small trimmed excerpts of real files, each for one thing reading the whole corpus
found (`test/hermes-realdata.test.js`). They are not among the fixtures above, which are each
converted whole with no reading options. Where a corpus's licence does not allow a copy here (IIP is
CC BY-NC 4.0; EHRI's only files with gazetteer links in a `<linkGrp>`, *The Sunflower*, are CC BY-NC-SA
4.0), the test builds an equivalent of its own instead, written in the test and named there.

| File | Where it comes from | Licence | What it exercises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `excerpts/isicily-ISic030001-header.xml` | [ISicily/ISicily](https://github.com/ISicily/ISicily), `inscriptions/ISic030001.xml`, commit `d3ebc63ff30b3b3b7359513292a5e7b01a05af7c` (a contract for the sale of a house, ed. Jonathan Prag). Trimmed: the teiHeader keeps the title and first editor, the publicationStmt, the msIdentifier and the history (unchanged); the text keeps only the edition div. | CC BY 4.0 (the repository's `licence.txt`, and the file's own `<licence>`) | A `provenance type="found" subtype="first-seen"` naming the museum the stone was given to, not its findspot; an `origPlace` with two place names and a `<geo>` |
| `excerpts/schnitzler-listplace-pmb365563.xml` | [arthur-schnitzler/schnitzler-briefe-data](https://github.com/arthur-schnitzler/schnitzler-briefe-data), `data/indices/listplace.xml`, commit `af1db1f88768df465963111b01931e3db9aa48d4`. Its teiHeader unchanged, and of its `<listPlace>` only the first place, `pmb365563` (Meidlinger Hauptstraße 56), unchanged. | MIT (the repository's `LICENSE`) | A listed place with its own `<location type="coords">` and two `<location type="located_in_place">` (the district and the street it is in), each with a `<placeName>` and a `<geo>`; every `<geo>` written with a comma for each decimal point |
| `excerpts/schnitzler-listplace-pmb364316.xml` | The same file as the row above (its teiHeader and its first place byte-identical to that excerpt's). Its teiHeader unchanged, and of its `<listPlace>` only the place `pmb364316` (Monte Viso), trimmed: its `<idno>`s of subtype `wikipedia` and `schnitzler-briefe` taken out, the rest unchanged. | MIT (the repository's `LICENSE`) | A listed place with idnos from four authorities (PMB, Wikidata, GND, GeoNames): one Headword about the preferred address (GeoNames, `hermes-preferred 1`), with an identity relation to each of the others |

Other openly licensed EpiDoc corpora were looked at for a place name with a ref in the text itself:
of I.Sicily's 5,138 inscriptions, 5,128 have a `placeName` with a ref, but nearly all of those are
in the teiHeader (where the stone came from); only three files have one in the text, and
ISic000934 is the one with both a name in the inscription and one in the commentary.

## The mapping

How `src/engine/hermes/tei.js` reads a TEI edition. Each place name in the text, for each place
address its ref points to, becomes one attestation-centric attestation about that place.

| In TEI | In PLATO | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<placeName>`, `<settlement>`, `<region>`, `<country>`, `<bloc>`, `<district>`, `<geogName>`, `<rs type="place">`, `<name type="place">`, in `<text>` | one attestation about the place its ref points to | In a file with no top-level `div type="edition"`, notes, commentary and translations included: the source is the edition, except a `<note>` marked as the editors' (`@type` editorial, commentary or translator, or a `@resp` that does not point to the work's own author: DEVELOPERS.md), which is the editors' words in any file, reported (`tei-place-editorial`, the example naming the note's resp or type) and converted only as below. In a file with one, every other top-level div (commentary, translation, apparatus, an introduction, a div with no type: any type, before the edition div or after it) and every `<note>` is the editors' words: reported (`tei-place-editorial`, with the part), converted only with the reading option `commentaryPlaces` (`--commentary-places`; on the page, *Read place names in the commentary and notes, as the editors' words*), then with the `formStatus` `plato:Editorial` (`EDITORIAL_IRI`), the part first in the locator, and the note "The editors' words, not the source's." A textpart inside the edition is the edition. In the teiHeader, a standOff or a facsimile, a place name is the edition's description of the document, and is reported, not converted; so is one in a `<listPerson>`, `<listOrg>`, `<listEvent>`, `<listBibl>`, `<person>`, `<org>`, `<event>` or `<bibl>` (`tei-place-in-record`, with its path), which describes that. One with a ref and no words (`tei-place-empty`), or of `type="ethnic"` (`tei-place-ethnic`, a people, not a place), is reported, not converted |
| `@ref`: a web address | `about` | Several addresses from different gazetteers are one place: one attestation about the preferred address (DEVELOPERS.md, "Preferred authorities, hermes-preferred 1"), with `identities` [{`subject` it, `object` each other address, `identityType` `unspecified`}], a note, and a warning once for each place (`tei-several-ids`); two from one gazetteer: ambiguous, reported (`tei-ref-ambiguous`), nothing converted; two forms of one address (http and https) are one. Pleiades, GeoNames and Wikidata addresses are put into each gazetteer's one form (DEVELOPERS.md, "Address rules"), with a note ("Place address given as … (rule …, hermes-addresses 1)"); part of a Pleiades place's record (`/places/<n>/<slug>`, `/json`, `#this`) is carried as given and reported |
| `@ref`: a prefixed pointer (`pl:579885`) | `about`, expanded through the header's `<prefixDef>` | The pattern must match everything after the prefix. No `prefixDef`, or one that gives no web address: reported |
| `@ref`: a local pointer (`#athens`) | `about`: the web-address `<idno>` of the `<place xml:id="athens">` in the same file | Several web addresses: as several in a ref (the preferred one, with identity relations; two from one gazetteer: `tei-ref-ambiguous`). None, or no such place: reported. A place later in the file is waited for |
| `@ref`: another file (`places.xml#x`), or a `urn:` | | Reported |
| The element's text, whitespace made single, notes left out, words broken over a line (`break="no"`) joined, a `<g>` whose ref or type names punctuation (`#interpunct`, a middle dot, a hedera) read as a space | `names[].toponym`, with `formStatus` `plato:Attested` | In a `<choice>`, `reg`, `expan`, `corr`; in an `<app>`, the `lem` |
| The form as printed, where a `<choice>` changed it (`orig`, `abbr`, `sic`) | `names[].sourceLabel` | Also where the place name is inside the `<choice>`, one in each part with the same ref: the part taken is the attestation, the printed one its `sourceLabel` |
| A place name wholly inside an `<rdg>`, or inside the part of a `<choice>` not taken (`orig`, `abbr`, `sic` beside `reg`, `expan`, `corr`) | | A variant reading: reported (`tei-variant`), not converted. A `<choice>` with one part takes it |
| An entity declared with its text in the file's own DOCTYPE (`<!ENTITY nbsp "&#160;">`) | its text | One whose text holds markup is refused where it is used. An external entity (`SYSTEM`, `PUBLIC`) is never fetched or read: using one stops the file |
| In a file whose DOCTYPE names an outside DTD (an external subset, as TEI P4's `"tei2.dtd"`, or an external parameter entity used in the internal subset, `%ISOgrk1;`): an entity the file does not declare, from the ISO sets (`&agr;`, `&eacute;`) | its character, from `src/vendor/iso-entities.json` (the W3C's ISO sets) | The file's own declarations win. Each set used is reported once, with each name and its count (`tei-entity-iso`, a warning). The DTD is never fetched. A name in neither (a library's own boilerplate, `&responsibility;`, `&fund.NEH;`) is left out, with nothing in its place, and reported once with each name and its count (`tei-entity-unknown`, a warning); a place name whose words, ref or key hold one, or a listed place whose address or headword does, is not converted (`tei-place-entity-unknown`, a loss); a source title or edition address (the idno used) holding one stops the file, naming it. In a file naming no outside DTD, any entity it does not declare is an error, named |
| The nearest `xml:lang`, inherited | `names[].language` | Only a language tag of two or three letters and its subtags; anything else is reported |
| TEI P4 (`<TEI.2>`, `<teiCorpus.2>`): `id`, `lang` | read as `xml:id`, `xml:lang` | A warning once (`tei-p4`). Only in P4: `<TEI>` with no namespace is P5 without its xmlns (`tei-no-namespace`, a warning), whose `id` and `lang` are not read. An element is TEI's when its namespace is the root's |
| TEI P4: `lang`, an IDREF to the header's `<language id>` | `names[].language`: the `<language>`'s `ident` where that is a language tag, else its id where that is one (`<language id="la">`) | Else `tei-lang-not-tag`, naming the `<language>` (`<language id="greek">Greek</language>`). In a `teiCorpus.2`, each `<TEI.2>`'s `<language>`s are its own (the same id may be Latin in one text and Greek in the next); the corpus header's hold for every text |
| TEI P4: a place name's `@reg`, the editors' regularised form | | Reported (`tei-reg`), not carried: the name is the text's. In P5 (where `@reg` is not TEI's), it is an attribute not read (`tei-attribute`), beside a ref or, on a name with a key and no ref, alone |
| TEI P4: a place name in Greek (its language's tag `grc` or `el`, or its `<language>` naming Greek) written in ASCII: Beta Code (`*)aqh=nai`) | the attestation, with no `names` | Not converted to Greek letters (decided 2026-10-01): reported, naming the string (`tei-p4-beta-code`), with a note |
| TEI P4: `<div1>`…`<div7>` | `citations[].locator`, as `<div>` ("book 1, chapter 1, section 1") | P4's divisions are numbered, and Perseus's top-level divs are books and chapters, never `type="edition"`: the edition rule never fires, and notes are the source's words unless marked as the editors' (`resp="ed"`) |
| `@key`, beside a ref | `notes` ("Key: …") | Never used for the address: the ref says which place |
| `@key`, with no ref | `about`, made with the pattern given for the key's prefix (the reading option `keyPatterns`, `{prefix: pattern}`: on the page, a row for each prefix in Reading options, its suggested pattern filled in and unticked until confirmed; `--key-pattern PREFIX=PATTERN`, or `--key-pattern PATTERN` for keys with no prefix), and `notes` ("Place address made from the key … with the pattern …") | The prefix is what comes before the key's first `:` or `,`; a key with neither has the prefix "". The rest must have the shape the pattern takes (digits for Pleiades and GeoNames, Q and digits for Wikidata, else `[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+`), else `tei-key-shape`; the address made goes through the address rules. A WHG pattern, or one for the prefix `whg`, is refused. With no pattern for its prefix, the place name is reported (`tei-place-no-ref`, with its key), and each prefix once (`tei-key-no-pattern`: its count, examples and a pattern to try). `teiKeyPrefixes(input)` gives the same for a page to prefill |
| `<div type n>` (for `type="textpart"`, its subtype), `<milestone unit n>`, `<pb n>`, `<l n>` or `<lb n>`, a `<note>`, `@xml:id` | `citations[].locator`, in words | "book 2, chapter 1, section 1, page 12", "edition, lines 2 to 4", "line 6", "commentary". In a file naming an outside DTD, an `n` holding an entity declared nowhere is left out of the locator, not given incomplete, and reported by element and line (`tei-locator-entity-unknown`) |
| The element and its line in the file | `notes` ("From TEI element <placeName> on line 180 of …") | The `xml:id` is never the attestation's `@id`: an edition can be revised under the same ids |
| teiHeader `titleStmt/title` (the `type="main"` one, else the first) | `citations[].source.title`, and the gazetteer's title ("Place names in …") | |
| `publicationStmt/idno type="URI"` (or `URL`), else `type="DOI"` | `citations[].source.@id` | None: a warning, and the source has only its title |
| `titleStmt/author` (else `editor`, with "(ed.)"), title, `publicationStmt/publisher`, `date` | `citations[].source.citation` | |
| `publicationStmt/availability/licence/@target` | `citations[].source.licence` | A licence in words only is reported |
| `sourceDesc/bibl` (or `biblStruct`, `biblFull`, `listBibl/bibl`), or `sourceDesc/msDesc/msIdentifier` | `citations[].source.derivedFrom`, by title | The original the edition was made from. Only the first; others are reported. A `sourceDesc/p` is not read |
| With `headerPlaces` (`--header-places`; on the page, *Read the places in the header (found at, made at), as the editors' words*): a place name with a ref in `provenance[@type="found"]` with no `@subtype`, or one meaning found (`discovered`, `excavated`, `found`) | an attestation with `formStatus` Editorial, the locator "teiHeader, provenance (found)", the note "The name is the editors' form, in the edition's header, not words of the source.", and `relations` [{`relatesTo` the object, `relationType` `plato:FindspotOf`, `relatedLabel` the title}] | The object: the msIdentifier's `idno type="URI"`, else the edition's `idno type="URI"`, never its DOI; neither: no relation, `tei-findspot-no-object`. No `relationLabel`: "found" is a code, not the source's words. Resolved at the end of the header, with the `prefixDef`s declared after it |
| With `headerPlaces`: a place name with a ref in `provenance[@type="found"]` with another `@subtype` (`first-seen`, `first-recorded`, `observed`, `transferred`…) | a plain attestation, the locator "teiHeader, provenance (found, <subtype>)", and a note naming the subtype; no relation | `tei-provenance-other`: it says where the object was seen or kept, not where it was found (I.Sicily ISic030001, given to the Ragusa museum) |
| A `<geo>` in a `provenance` or `origin` in the teiHeader | | Reported (`tei-header-geo`), with or without `headerPlaces`; not carried |
| With `headerPlaces`: a place name with a ref in `origin` (an `origPlace` with a ref, or one inside it) | the same, with the locator "teiHeader, origin" and a note that it is the place of origin; no relation | `tei-header-origin`: PLATO has no relation for a place of origin |
| A `<geo>`, `<location>`, `<idno>` or `<note>` inside a place name | | Not part of the name ("Beth Loya<geo>31.56,34.93</geo>" is "Beth Loya"). A `<geo>` in a place name in the text is reported (`tei-place-geo`), once each, not carried |
| `<listPlace>/<place>`: its names, its `<location>` | | Reported once per place, unless the reading option `listPlaces` is on (*Read the list of places* on the page, `--list-places` on the command line) |
| With `listPlaces`: a `<place>` with a web-address `<idno>` | one attestation for that address (several different ones: about the preferred one, with identity relations to the others, `tei-several-ids`; two from one gazetteer: ambiguous, `tei-listplace-ambiguous`, nothing converted; two forms of one address count as one): its first name as `names[0]` with `formStatus` `plato:Headword`, the locator "list of places, place <xml:id>", the note "From TEI element <place xml:id=…> on line …" | Its other names are reported (`tei-listplace-variant`); no web address: reported (`tei-listplace-no-address`). In the teiHeader, it waits for the end of the header (the header's title, address and `geoDecl` may come after it); in `<text>` or `<back>`, it is converted where the place ends |
| `<listPlace>/<place>/<location type="located_in_place">` (a type that says the location is another place's: `located_in`, `parent`, `part_of`, `within`, `in_place`, `broader`), and the names and `<geo>` in it | | Not this place's location or names: reported (`tei-listplace-geo-other-place`). Only a name that is the `<place>`'s own child is one of its names |
| With `listPlaces`: `<location>/<geo>` "lat long" or "lat, long", or with a comma for each decimal point and a space between ("48,177598 16,329723") | `geometries[]`: `reprPoint` [long, lat], a GeoJSON Point, `sourceLabel` as written | Only where the place's address is on the edition's own site (the host of its `idno type="URI"`; so never for an edition known only by its DOI), else `tei-listplace-geo-gazetteer`; only with no `geoDecl` or one in WGS84 (TEI's default), else `tei-listplace-geo-datum`; out of range, not two numbers, or commas that could mean more than one thing ("48,1,16,3"): `tei-listplace-geo-invalid` |
| `<listPlace>/<place>/<linkGrp>/<link type="normal" target="…">` (or a `<link>` with no type), as EHRI writes a place's gazetteer links | each target that is a web address, read as an `<idno>` is (the same rules: `placeAddress`, several as several idnos) | A `<link>` of another type (EHRI's `type="desc"`, a Wikipedia article), or a target that is not a web address, is reported (`tei-place-content`) |
| `<listPlace>/<place>`: a `<desc>`, a `<note>`, an idno that is not an address, any other child | | Reported, once for each place and part |
| A WHG address: `place:<ns>:<id>` (with no `prefixDef` for `place`), `whgazetteer.org/entity/place:…` | `about`: `https://w3id.org/whg/id/place:<ns>:<id>`, and `notes` ("Place address given as … (rule whg-record-id, hermes-addresses 1)") | Also for an address from a `prefixDef` or a listPlace idno. A declared `prefixDef` for `place` wins. A `/places/<n>/portal` address with n below 12,345,678, or one on dev.whgazetteer.org, is reported, not converted |
| Any other attribute of a place name (`@cert`, `@type` on `<placeName>`, `@resp`, …) or of a `<place>` | | Reported, once for each attribute and value. `@cert` is not taken for certaintyLevel: TEI does not say what it is certain of |
